investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-23T15:47–15:48Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first network hop to the swarm backend, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever collected, and all contract assertions remain unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. The production API returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" on every attempt. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner or its configuration. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is confirmed only at the eval layer.

possibleCauses: Primary: The swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production API to return 502 on all POST /api/agents requests.

Secondary: A network routing or security-group change between the production API and the swarm ELB blocked outbound connectivity to the ELB endpoint, producing a connection-level error surfaced as 502.
Tertiary: The swarm gateway was undergoing a deployment or scaling event that temporarily removed all healthy targets from the ELB, causing a transient 502 window that coincided with the eval run.
Lower probability: The ELB DNS record was stale or the ELB itself was deleted/replaced, making the endpoint permanently unreachable until reconfigured.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-23T15:47–15:48Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents during agent provisioning. investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. The production API returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)" on every attempt. Tertiary: The swarm gateway was undergoing a deployment or scaling event that temporarily removed all healthy targets from the ELB, causing a transient 502 window that coincided with the eval run.
Lower probability: The ELB DNS record was stale or the ELB itself was deleted/replaced, making the endpoint permanently unreachable until reconfigured.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Agent Provisioning Evals
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-23T15:47–15:48Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the POST /api/agents call before any agent is created, no evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were ever populated, causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning path — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This upstream failure prevented agent creation entirely, which is the prerequisite step for all three remote-agents checks. The failure is localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no evidence of a broader platform outage or user-traffic incident is present in the supplied packet.
